original_query: SELECT COUNT(C) FILTER (WHERE g_0_f_1), COUNT(D) FILTER (WHERE g_0_f_0) FROM (SELECT SAL > 1000 AS C, SAL < 500 AS D, GROUPING(SAL > 1000, SAL < 500) = 0 AND SAL > 1000 AS g_0_f_0, GROUPING(SAL > 1000, SAL < 500) = 0 AND SAL < 500 AS g_0_f_1 FROM EMP GROUP BY SAL > 1000, SAL < 500) AS t3
rewritten_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sal < 500), COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sal > 1000) FROM emp

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: GROUPING(...) = 0 is always true in a simple GROUP BY, so g_0_f_0/g_0_f_1 reduce to SAL > 1000 and SAL < 500.
Eliminate the inner grouped subquery and outer FILTER aggregation: each outer COUNT can only be 0 or 1, so the whole query reduces to two existence checks on emp.
Replace full-table GROUP BY over 45M rows with two EXISTS subqueries, which can short-circuit as soon as a matching row is found; an index on emp(sal) will make this highly efficient.
Since COUNT over a single qualifying group is always 1, fold the output into constants 1/0 via CASE WHEN EXISTS.
